title: Chromatic Energy Transfer Studio
description: A mystical studio where a GlassVaseFlowers arrangement and a ShaderBall share a finite pool of chromatic energy. The user redistributes color channels (R, G, B) between the two objects using sliders and click interactions, with a conservation law ensuring total energy remains constant. Undo/redo support lets the user explore and revert complex multi-channel transfers.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap/CDN) that loads GlassVaseFlowers.glb and ShaderBall.glb side by side on a reflective dark platform. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 2, 6) looking at origin, with OrbitControls. Add an HDR-style environment using PMREMGenerator with a simple procedural gradient, plus a directional light and two colored point lights. Place the vase at (-1.5, 0, 0) and the shader ball at (1.5, 0, 0). Implement a chromatic energy conservation system: a total energy budget of 3.0 is split across R, G, B channels (each starting at 0.5 per object, totaling 1.0 per channel). Display three horizontal sliders (R, G, B) in an HTML overlay panel. Each slider ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 and controls how much of that channel goes to the vase; the shader ball automatically receives the remainder (1.0 minus vase value). Apply these color values as emissive tint multipliers on all meshes of each model using MeshStandardMaterial. When the user clicks on either object (via raycasting), cycle that object through three blend modes: Additive, Multiply, Screen, which changes how the emissive color combines with the base albedo. Show the current blend mode as a floating label above each object using CSS2DRenderer. Implement a full undo/redo stack (at least 20 states) tracking all slider values and blend mode selections. Add keyboard shortcuts Z for undo and Y for redo, plus on-screen buttons. Each state change (slider release or click-to-cycle) pushes to the stack. Add a particle system of small glowing orbs that flow from the object losing energy to the one gaining it whenever a slider changes, with particle color matching the transferred channel. Display a HUD showing the total energy per object and per channel to verify conservation. The interaction sequence involves adjusting 3 sliders, clicking objects to cycle blend modes multiple times, and using undo/redo, totaling 10-14 meaningful steps.
